$comment:
How a sampled patch of the real Earth becomes one of this game's eleven terrains. This file holds the RULES and nothing about any region: a thing the sampler measured goes in a samples file; a thing a person knows about a place goes in the map's commission. Change a number here and every real-Earth board reclassifies on its next draw.

A hex is about 17,000 square kilometres, so every rule is a rule about an average over that much ground. Elevation decides hills and mountains first, because relief beats climate; climate (the Koeppen-Geiger class of most of the hex's land) decides what grows on the rest.

thresholds.$landPct: A hex is land when at least this share of its sample points are above sea level. Lower keeps more small islands and fatter coasts; higher drowns them.
thresholds.$shelfDepthM: Sea shallower than this (the continental shelf) is shallow water; deeper is deep water.
thresholds.$relief: A hex is mountain if its average height is at least meanM, or its high ground (the 90th percentile) reaches p90M AND climbs reliefM above its average. Hills likewise.

climate.$comment: Koeppen-Geiger class -> terrain, for ground that is neither hills nor mountain. Steppe and Mediterranean scrub are grassland because that is what the game's grassland means: open ground more grass than tree.
